questions.question:
Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

47 : 58 : 71
questions.solution:
The Logic here is as follows:

**Step 1 → 1st Number**

**Step 2 → 1st Number + (digit sum of 1st number) = 2ⁿd number**

**Step 3 → 2ⁿd number + (digit sum of 2ⁿd number) = 3rd number**

**In **47 : 58 : 71

Step 1 → 47

Step 2 → 47 + (4 + 7) = 47 + 11 = 58 = 2ⁿd number

Step 3 → 58 + (5 + 8) = 58 + 13 = 71 = 3rd number

Similarly,

**72 : 81 : 90**

**Step 1 → 72**

**Step 2 → 72 + (7 + 2) = 72 + 9 = 81 = 2ⁿd number**

**Step 3 → 81 + (8 + 1) = 81 + 9 = 90 = 3rd number**

Hence, the correct answer is **"(****72 : 81 : 90****)".**

questions.question: The District Transport Authority has started special bus services for college going students. One bus starts from village P. The number of girls in the bus is one-fourth of the number of boys. In village Q, 20 boys leave the bus at their college stop and ten girls enter the bus. Now the number of boys and girls is equal. How many students enter the bus in the beginning?
questions.solution:
Let,

**Number of girls = G**

**Number of boys = B**

**At village P**

Number of girls in the bus is one-fourth of the number of boys so,

=> G = 1/4B

=> 4G = B

**At village Q**

20 boys leave the bus at their college stop and ten girls enter the bus.

Number of girls = G + 10

Number of boys = B - 20

Now the number of boys and girls is equal

=> G + 10 = B – 20

∵ 4G = B

So,

=> G + 10 = 4G – 20

=> 4G - 4 = 20 + 10

=> 3G = 30

=> G = 10

∵ 4G = B

So, B = 4 × 10

B = 40

Total number of students enter the bus in the beginning = B + G = 10 + 40 = 50

Hence, Total number of students enter the bus in the beginning is **“50”**.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some dogs are bulls.

All bulls are donkeys.

**Conclusions:**

I. All dogs are donkeys.

II. Some donkeys are dogs.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

questions.solution:
**Statements:**

Some dogs are bulls.

All bulls are donkeys.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47f539de0eeae7372a26bcf1557e3a74f27c3fc963e941800a75fef1c06a3406.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. All dogs are donkeys → False (It is possible but not definite)

II. Some donkeys are dogs → True (because some dogs are bulls and all bulls are donkeys so definitely some donkeys are also dogs)

Hence, “**Only conclusions II follows”.**
